utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon to Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-97-24-A, The Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I please have the appearances of the parties. For the Prosecution, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, Mr. Xavier Tracol, and our case manager today is Ms. Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Stakic, I just wanted to make sure that you can hear me and you can hear the proceedings in a language that you understand. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Yes, I can follow you in a language I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You may be seated, Mr. Stakic. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference called in accordance with 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires that a Status Conference be convened within 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. Mr. Stakic, do you have any issues which you would like to raise in relation to your detention? Do you have any concerns regarding your mental or physical well being? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for asking me. At this point in time, I have no comments or criticisms to make with respect to the conditions in the Detention Unit, neither do I have any issues with respect to my physical and mental condition. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. We will now turn to other relevant matters to this appeal. The Prosecution has filed before the Appeals Chamber, a status report in which they have indicated that are still in the process of identifying and disclosing Rule 68 material. In that report, the Prosecutor says that they disclosed on the 2nd of December, 2003, four pages of transcript of the witness's interview with the Prosecution in a related case. And it is currently conducting an electronic search for post-judgement document which may be relevant to the appeal. Once that search is completed, the material identified as relevant will be reviewed by the Prosecutor, and any Rule 68 material identified will be disclosed. The Prosecutor has also advised the Appeals Chamber that investigations remain ongoing in related cases concerning the Municipality of Prijedor and that there is the possibility of obtaining further information that may require disclosure from those investigations. Mr. Farrell, could you please give some indication as to when you think this process will be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The material that we have reviewed at the moment is the material from after the judgement, post-judgement. And it probably will take about two months, I think, from today to review that. There's quite a number of material that has to be-- as you're aware, we search it electronically, then we narrow it down to relevant material, then we review it for Rule 68. So that process, I think will probably take at least, let's say, two months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Do you have adequate staff to --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes, I think we can deal with it in that time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Does the Defence have any comment on the status report of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only comment we have is that we are not aware about these four pages. I found only the translated version of the judgement, but I didn't find these four pages of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Could I ask Farrell to clarify the situation on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: It's my understanding that it was sent -- I can speak with counsel afterwards, and if he didn't receive it, I'll ensure you get it today. It's my understanding it was disclosed and sent to you. It's a Rule 68 matter. It was sent by letter December 2nd 2003, and it attached a disclosure receipt and some material to it. That's what I'm speaking to. I'm not sure that was your understanding, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It may be that it was faxed to my office fax number, and at that time I was here in Den Haag. But we don't have any problems meeting with the Prosecution after this Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's mine. I'll make sure we make a copy and give it to you immediately afterwards. No problem, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence has also recently filed another request for an extension of time for the filing of its appeal brief. This was filed on the 17th of December. That was yesterday. On the 30th of October, I granted an extension of time allowing the Defence to file its brief on or before the 6th of January, 2004. In its motion requesting a further extension, the Defence states that due to the volume of material on the electronic database to which it was given access by the Prosecutor on the 24th of November and due to the fact that the judgement of the Trial Chamber was only made available to Dr. Stakic in B/C/S language on 9 of December, it is not possible for it to meet that deadline. It seeks a further extension of between 30 and 45 days for the filing of that brief, and then a motion under Rule 115 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. At this time, I would like to ask Mr. Farrell whether the Prosecution is able to indicate its position on the motion by the Defence for an extension. Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two issues that are raised in the motion, as you've indicated. One relates to the search for additional evidence, and the other relates to the appeal brief. The normal practice, as you're fully aware, Mr. President, is that the additional evidence isn't related to the appeal brief. The appeal brief is on the record and any additional evidence is filed separately. In that regard, although obviously there's an onerous burden in light of the workload of my learned colleagues, what I would suggest to Your Honour, in my submission, is that we keep those two process separate. But for the appeal brief that's due on January 6th, the Prosecution has no objection to a reasonable extension of time, in light of the fact that the B/C/S version of the judgement came a week or so late. My understanding from your previous decision was that the reasonable amount of time included the time for them to have the B/C/S version. So since it's been delayed a short period of time, we have no objection to a short extension of time to take that into consideration for them filing their appeal brief and that that's not dependent on a review of the additional evidence. That's just on the record. So whatever reasonable period of time it is for them to file their appeal brief, we have no objection to that in light of that consideration. The other issue is whether or not there's an extension of time for the 115 motion because of the additional evidence. I note that the 115 motion, if there was to be one, was actually due on October the 14th. So it's now already two months passed that. And even though there has been access to the disclosure database in November, any motion should have been filed long before they even got access to that database. The database itself isn't a basis, in the Prosecution's submission, for why there wasn't something filed on the 14th or an extension of time, of course, sought on the 14th. Also, the database doesn't alleviate the Prosecution from reviewing and disclosing Rule 68 at this stage, with the present rules the way they are, so though of course my learned colleagues are at liberty to review the database in case they find anything which will assist them to continue to do investigations and find new evidence, that database in and of itself isn't, in my view, a basis for claiming that there is material there they haven't received that would be Rule 68. What I would propose is that with respect to the appeal brief, a reasonable period of time, in light of the delay in getting the B/C/S version. In relation to the 115 material, since the date is already past, and since they'll need to seek leave, what I would suggest is once they have Rule 115 material that they intend to file - and it's not clear to me whether they do or they don't from their motion - once they have any Rule 115 material that they would seek to file, since they're already past the deadline, they should just bring it at that time with a motion seeking leave, at that time explaining why it wasn't available when the deadline was due and we'll address it then when they bring the 115 motion. That way we can dispose of the motion for the appeal brief. That can be dealt with in a reasonable period of time. I appreciate, of course, it's over the holidays, so I don't want my learned colleagues to have to work too extensively during that period. So a reasonable period for the appeal brief is acceptable to us, and then in relation to the 115, once they have had a chance to get their 115 material together, they can file a motion at that time indicating why they weren't able to file it back on October 14th. I think that would be the most reasonable way to deal with it. Unless you have any questions, that would my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Before turning to the Defence, I see you're already in the holiday gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President, I leave that to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: In a benevolent mood.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: After the previous cases are done, I'm already thinking of the next steps, toward the holidays. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Turning to the Defence, as I have indicated, the motion for an extension also seeks an extension of time for the filing of a motion under Rule 115, under Rule 115(A), as you all know, motions for additional evidence on appeal must be submitted within 75 days of the date of judgement. The judgement was issued on the 31st of July 2003, which means that motions under Rule 115 were due on the 14th of October. Under the Tribunal precedents, a request for an extension of time to file a Rule 115 motion should have been filed by that date as well. I recall that the Defence filed a motion for an extension of time to file its appeal brief on that day, which I granted, but neither that motion nor my order mentioned Rule 115 at the time. And I would like to ask the Defence counsel why it has -- why has the Defence waited so long to request an extension for the 115 filing?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. John Ostojic on behalf of Dr. Stakic. To address the Court's question specifically, we believe that it would not have been prudent at that time to seek an extension of time and claim that there's any basis for 115 unless we actually had the material. Mr. Lukic has specifically conducted through the electronic version of the database provided to us research and has found some material. We thought it would be premature to anticipate, A, that the Prosecution failed in their obligation and duty to give us all the material, and B, we did not want to get a response from the Prosecution saying that we're filing for an extension of time but have no basis for an extension of time. If we had the documents and needed additional time to review them, naturally we would have filed it timely and within the deadlines in the Rules. Since we didn't have it, we thought that it was inappropriate to file at that time because we would be asking for something that we had no knowledge if were going to pursue. I'd like to also address a complicated situation with respect to these documents. The Municipality of Prijedor is unique in the sense that the searches that were conducted in the Prijedor Municipality allowed the representative parties, the Prosecutor namely, to seize and take away all the documents in the municipality, in the police station, and in various barracks. Copies were not made at the site. Those were taken by the Prosecution. The Defence does not have access and has never had access to all those searches that were done. Hopefully now with this database, that will be clarified and we have an avenue to review all the documents and we will try to, if necessary, seek leave at the appropriate time attaching the documents and our arguments as to why we think its appropriate to have those documents before the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Any additional comments, Mr. Farrell?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Just in light of the fact if we're going to disclose if there is anything within the next two months any Rule 68 material if we find any, and in light of fact that they have had the opportunity to review, maybe the best way, if I may suggest, would be that the Court indicate at some point in time that there be a notice from the Defence indicating if they have any material. They don't have to, of course, inform the Prosecution what it is, just to indicate if they have any material and the time frame that it would take for that material to be filed. That may assist the Court in giving a scheduling order, but it also would assist in ensuring we have a schedule for the proceeding in this matter. Since at this stage, obviously, we're not aware of what's coming, and the Defence still indicates their intention to search. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: The Defence. I suppose you have no problems with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, we are just before the judicial recess, and the filing date which was previously established, as you all know, was the 6th of January. I believe that it would be in the interest of all the parties that I would rule on the motion for extension now, so you know where you stand. Having heard both parties, I feel that it is in the interest of justice to grant a certain extension of time to file the appeal brief. However, given the fact that Dr. Stakic received the translation of the Trial Chamber judgement on the 9th of December, and is therefore able to consult with counsel about the content of the brief, I am not persuaded that an extension of 45 days is warranted. I would grant today a more limited extension beyond the extension already granted, and I will grant, therefore, the Defence that the Defence appeal brief shall be filed on or before February 1, 2004. So for the appeal brief, on or before February 1. As for the matter of the Rule 115 motion, I am still somewhat troubled despite the explanations given by the failure of the Defence to raise this issue in a timely manner, particularly given the finding of a prior motion for extension. Normally, that would be sufficient ground for denying this part of the request. However, given that the process of disclosure is ongoing and that the Prosecution expects to disclose further Rule 68 material, the interests of justice suggest that I should nonetheless consider this request as though it were made in a timely fashion. As it is the holiday season, I will grant the same extension for the Rule 115 as for the appeal brief. The Defence may file, therefore, a motion under Rule 115 on or before February 1, 2004. I remind the Defence counsel, however, that the Tribunal will not take kindly to belated applications for extensions of time. I would also like to remind both of the parties that the appeals proceedings must be conducted as expeditiously as possible. If the Prosecutor can assist the Defence in conducting its searches with the electronic database, it would be in the interests of all that it does so. A written order setting forth my ruling on this motion will be filed this afternoon or, at the latest, tomorrow. Do either the parties wish to raise any other issues? Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. If there are no other issues, I thank the parties for their attendance, with a Merry Christmas and Happy New Year, and call the proceedings to a close.
